Section B: Methodology — How UIO Is Calculated
Step 1 — Collect vehicle sales data
For each country/distributor, gather annual unit sales by model and calendar year (vintage cohort). Source: IML shipment records, ITUK car park data.
Step 2 — Assign vehicle category
Classify each cohort as CV (Developed), CV (Emerging), or LCV based on model type and market. ISZE Europe markets = CV Developed. LCV = separate curve.
Step 3 — Apply survival rates
For projection year Y and vintage cohort V: UIO(Y,V) = units_sold(V) × survival_rate(Y−V). If age > max rate age, survival = 0 (vehicle scrapped).
Step 4 — Sum across cohorts
Total UIO for year Y = Σ UIO(Y,V) across all vintage years V. This gives the estimated number of Isuzu vehicles still in operation.
Step 5 — Forecast new sales
For future years, add projected new sales cohorts from the IML mid-term plan (FY2025–FY2030) to the calculation.
LCV note

LCV survival rates use the 12-year window model. The IML LCV shipment forecast currently extends to FY2029 only (CY2028). FY2030 / CY2029 data is pending — see '1.UIO Overview' for clarification note.
Section C: Formula Logic

UIO(Projection Year Y) = Σ [ Units Sold in Vintage Year V  ×  SurvivalRate(Y − V) ]  where SurvivalRate(age) comes from Section A above.  Example: N75 units sold in 2015 = 621 units.  In projection year 2025, vehicle age = 10 years → CV Developed survival = 55%.  UIO contribution = 621 × 0.55 = 342 units.  Full ITUK calculation is shown step-by-step in sheet "4. Section B: Methodology — How UIO Is Calculated
Step 1 — Collect vehicle sales data
For each country/distributor, gather annual unit sales by model and calendar year (vintage cohort). Source: IML shipment records, ITUK car park data.
Step 2 — Assign vehicle category
Classify each cohort as CV (Developed), CV (Emerging), or LCV based on model type and market. ISZE Europe markets = CV Developed. LCV = separate curve.
Step 3 — Apply survival rates
For projection year Y and vintage cohort V: UIO(Y,V) = units_sold(V) × survival_rate(Y−V). If age > max rate age, survival = 0 (vehicle scrapped).
Step 4 — Sum across cohorts
Total UIO for year Y = Σ UIO(Y,V) across all vintage years V. This gives the estimated number of Isuzu vehicles still in operation.
Step 5 — Forecast new sales
For future years, add projected new sales cohorts from the IML mid-term plan (FY2025–FY2030) to the calculation.
LCV note

LCV survival rates use the 12-year window model. The IML LCV shipment forecast currently extends to FY2029 only (CY2028). FY2030 / CY2029 data is pending — see '1.UIO Overview' for clarification note.
Section C: Formula Logic

UIO(Projection Year Y) = Σ [ Units Sold in Vintage Year V  ×  SurvivalRate(Y − V) ]  where SurvivalRate(age) comes from Section A above.  Example: N75 units sold in 2015 = 621 units.  In projection year 2025, vehicle age = 10 years → CV Developed survival = 55%.  UIO contribution = 621 × 0.55 = 342 units.  Full ITUK calculation is shown step-by-step in sheet "4. Section A: Survival Rates by Vehicle Type & Age
Source: LCV UIO (November 2025)_EU_Study_Imit.xlsx — 'Survival Ratio' sheet | These rates represent the proportion of a vehicle cohort remaining in operation after N years.

Section B: Methodology — How UIO Is Calculated
Step 1 — Collect vehicle sales data
For each country/distributor, gather annual unit sales by model and calendar year (vintage cohort). Source: IML shipment records, ITUK car park data.
Step 2 — Assign vehicle category
Classify each cohort as CV (Developed), CV (Emerging), or LCV based on model type and market. ISZE Europe markets = CV Developed. LCV = separate curve.
Step 3 — Apply survival rates
For projection year Y and vintage cohort V: UIO(Y,V) = units_sold(V) × survival_rate(Y−V). If age > max rate age, survival = 0 (vehicle scrapped).
Step 4 — Sum across cohorts
Total UIO for year Y = Σ UIO(Y,V) across all vintage years V. This gives the estimated number of Isuzu vehicles still in operation.
Step 5 — Forecast new sales
For future years, add projected new sales cohorts from the IML mid-term plan (FY2025–FY2030) to the calculation.
LCV note

LCV survival rates use the 12-year window model. The IML LCV shipment forecast currently extends to FY2029 only (CY2028). FY2030 / CY2029 data is pending — see '1.UIO Overview' for clarification note.
Section C: Formula Logic

UIO(Projection Year Y) = Σ [ Units Sold in Vintage Year V  ×  SurvivalRate(Y − V) ]  where SurvivalRate(age) comes from Section A above.  Example: N75 units sold in 2015 = 621 units.  In projection year 2025, vehicle age = 10 years → CV Developed survival = 55%.  UIO contribution = 621 × 0.55 = 342 units.  Full ITUK calculation is shown step-by-step in sheet "4.
